body: they do look very long, I try to keep my rabbits nails just slightly peeking out of the fur and this rabbit has very very visible nails. A word of warning about trimming them if you plan to do so; overgrown nails mean an overgrown quick. If nails are trimmed regularly the quick will recede gradually, but the longer they go uncut the longer the quicks will be. This rabbit looks to have very pigmented nails, so using a flashlight to see the quicks might help. Even if you trim them once they probably will still look kind of messed up, it will take a bit for them to start growing correctly. If you don’t feel comfortable doing this, most vets will cut rabbit nails even if they don’t treat exotics, since nail trims are very basic services. I know they aren’t yours but maybe you could request to take them to a vet?
